text.text: Outbound: how is a draft claimed so a double click can't send it twice?
New engineers · The owner's Send click, the sendAction server action, and the atomic UPDATE…RETURNING claim in Postgres.

Key: frames = trust/deployment zones; box = runtime actor/process; cylinder = stored state. Arrows: caller → recipient, response
included; solid = sync. Flow type is also written on each arrow.

One UPDATE sets status 'sending' and
saves any edited body/subject, WHERE
id matches, direction 'out', status in
draft/failed. No returned row → skipped:
'Already sent or no longer a draft.'

The claim stops a second click or tab
from sending. Later guards reset the
row to failed (no person, daily limit) or
skipped (closed stage, already replied).
Delivery is not guaranteed.

A row stuck in 'sending' can't be
claimed again; only draft/failed rows
qualify. The health check flags LinkedIn
rows stuck over 3h. The code shows no
automatic recovery for email.
Outside this view: Guard checks, Gmail/LinkedIn delivery and reply detection after claim; Drafting, enrollment, cron jobs and the LinkedIn browser worker.
